$comment: The package ledger. Every source file in this repo belongs to exactly one
package, and scripts/check-packages.mjs fails if that stops being true.
This file exists because of a diagnosis, not a preference: reepub started
(2026-05-28) with the right division — Swift for what only Swift can do
(Vision OCR), Node for assembly. It drifted twice. On 2026-06-14 the app
needed to be offline and self-sufficient, so assembly was rebuilt in Swift;
that is where 'one implementation' broke. Between 2026-07-30 and 08-01 five
more modules appeared, all Node-only, in three days.
Nobody chose that. Sessions without memory of how the repo grew kept
building in whichever direction was convenient, and Node is the convenient
one. A ledger a machine reads is the only kind that survives that, which is
why 'sources' is enforced rather than documented.
Decision 2026-08-02 (see HANDOFF.md): the assembly core moves to Swift,
because Vision OCR cannot leave it and offline quality is what the product
stands on. 'target' records where each file is headed; 'sources' records
where it actually is today. They are allowed to disagree — that gap IS the
migration. What is not allowed is a file belonging to neither.
Shape 2026-08-04 (see HANDOFF.md, and reef/docs/SPEC-pagetile-vision.md):
the pipeline has one junction and it has never been named. PDF becomes OCR
JSON, which becomes structured chapters, which become an EPUB. That middle
term is an intermediate representation with one consumer, so nothing forced
it to be honest. Naming it splits the repo into 'ingest' (anything -> the
book model) and 'render' (the book model -> a file someone reads), which is
the same adapter-in/target-out shape pagetile locked on 2026-07-15.
'layer' below records which side of that junction a package is on. It is a
direction, not a migration: no file has to move for it to be true, and the
next thing built is expected to land on the side the ledger says it belongs.
A package with no layer is not part of the pipeline.
Nothing enforces 'layer', and that is deliberate rather than unfinished. A
gate that forbade an ingest from reaching a render would fail today, which
would make it a migration order rather than a direction — and this file
already carries the distinction between a promise CI keeps and a record that
only tells you where things stand (PRINCIPLES §6). 'layer' is a record. It
becomes a promise the day the book model is a real boundary, not before.
The book model travels as markdown, not as a library: the shared thing is
the FORMAT, and each language parses it for itself (ruled 2026-08-04). That
is only safe because the format gets a written spec and a fixture corpus
both sides are checked against — without those it is §6's trap again.

scan-ocr.purpose: PDF → one JSON line per recognised text line, with bounding boxes. Apple Vision. No EPUB knowledge whatsoever.
scan-ocr.layerNote: PDF -> OCR JSON. The only ingest that starts from something that is not text.

cjk-specimen.purpose: Specimen text for CJK typography fixtures, plus the list of places CJK layout is known to break — each hazard carrying what it is for and where the evidence lives. A fixture that never touches a boundary proves nothing when it passes.

epub-kit.purpose: The assembly core: package document, navigation document, NCX, chapter XHTML, cover. The one implementation, per decision A. Ships a CLI so the Node side can drive it instead of keeping an assembler of its own. Also holds the book format itself — BookMarkdown.swift parses and serialises the markdown the book model travels as, and the book-md CLI prints its data columns so a machine can compare it against a second implementation (scripts/check-book-format.mjs).
epub-kit.layerNote: Book model -> EPUB 3, and the book model's own on-disk form. The maintained assembler, and now the reference parser for the format the junction is named after.

epub-text.purpose: XML and text plumbing: escaping, serialisation, entity decoding, pictograph stripping. Seven modules import it and every one of them is alive.
epub-text.layerNote: Plumbing both sides call. Not a stage.

epub-binder.purpose: Emits package documents from Node for heal / merge / web-ingest. Transitional by construction: it is the second assembler, and the boundary gate lists it as a known one until those callers drive epub-kit instead.
epub-binder.target: epub-kit — Node tools should call the Swift binary rather than emit their own <package>
epub-binder.layerNote: Book model -> EPUB 3, Node side. Second assembler; see target.

epub-doctor.purpose: Operates on finished EPUBs: validate, heal, merge. Never touches OCR, never rasterises a cover — which is what keeps its dependency budget to one library.
epub-doctor.layerNote: Takes an EPUB and gives back an EPUB — it is an ingest and a render at once, which is why it is the piece that most wants the book model to exist.

epub-cover.purpose: The cover as text, with no browser in it: which layout an edition gets, the XHTML page that shows the finished image, and where an English title breaks. merge needs the cover PAGE for every book that has one — including a cover it merely carried across — so this half must be reachable without installing Chromium.
epub-cover.target: moves to epub-kit (Swift), which emits the same HTML for both rasterisers
epub-cover.layerNote: Typesetting for a render target, not a stage of its own.

epub-raster.purpose: Turns the typeset cover into pixels, and redraws pictographs as engravings. Chromium and sharp live here and nowhere else — this is the package a repair tool must be able to do without.
epub-raster.target: one of two rasterisers over one typesetter; the app's is WKWebView

web-ingest.purpose: A web page reduced to structure: strip layout, translate classes, dehydrate images. The base a web→md exporter would sit on.
web-ingest.layerNote: Web pages -> chapters. Second ingest; predates the junction being named.

ocr-builder-node.purpose: The Node path from OCR output to EPUB, and the paragraph heuristics only it uses. This is the ONLY code genuinely duplicated by EpubBuilder.swift.
ocr-builder-node.allowedDependenciesNote: cheerio arrives through validator.js; builder.js imports nothing external itself
ocr-builder-node.freezeCondition: flips to "frozen" when the CLI builds through epub-kit. Kept, not strangled — but kept as a FILE, never as a documented way to use reepub.
ocr-builder-node.layerNote: OCR JSON -> chapters. The Node half of what scan-ocr feeds.

app.purpose: The product. SwiftUI, offline, consumes scan-ocr + epub-kit.

cli.purpose: Thin surfaces over the cores: local web UI, the web→EPUB entry point, the image optimizer.

_tests.purpose: Suites. Not a shipped package; claimed here so no test file counts as unowned.

_tooling.purpose: Repo-level guards, fetchers and the release build. Not shipped.

cover-probe.purpose: An instrument, not a product: renders HTML offscreen with WKWebView and writes a PNG, so the question 'does WKWebView lay out the cover like Chromium' has a measurement instead of an opinion. Findings in docs/wkwebview-cover-parity.md.
cover-probe.layerNote: Measures a render target. Not on any path a book takes.
